headline: TUDOR HITS 44.38 g/t Au AND 440 g/t Ag IN NEW PORPHYRY ZONE — TREATY CREEK SYSTEM EXPANDS BEYOND PERFECTSTORM
snippet: Tudor Gold Corp. (TSXV: TUD) released September 17 results from ten holes at Treaty Creek's Perfectstorm Zone in BC's Golden Triangle — best hole PS-26-28 returned 44.38 g/t gold and 440 g/t silver over 0.80 metres within a newly confirmed PSP copper-gold-silver-molybdenum porphyry system, while a companion near-surface PSE epithermal gold zone was verified through three additional holes; surface sampling 1.2 km northwest returned up to 13.54 g/t gold, and two drills remain active on priority targets with additional results pending. Treaty Creek adjoins Seabridge's KSM and Newmont's Brucejack.

headline: PAN GLOBAL DRILLS 83M AT 1.74 g/t Au IN SPAIN — WIDEST INTERCEPT YET ALSO HITS COPPER, COBALT AND PLATINUM
snippet: Pan Global Resources (TSXV: PGZ) released September 17 results from drillhole PVD16 at the Providencia target within its 100%-owned Cármenes Project in northern Spain — 83 metres at 1.74 g/t gold from 9 metres depth, including 4.88 g/t gold over 9 metres, 12.57 g/t gold over 2 metres and a peak of 32.2 g/t gold over 0.5 metres — the widest high-grade intersection yet in the Phase 3 program; the hole also returned copper, cobalt, nickel, platinum and palladium mineralization on the Rio Narcea Gold Belt, a historically underexplored corridor in northwestern Spain.

headline: SIX JUNIOR MINERS JOIN GDXJ TONIGHT — PASSIVE BUYING HITS GOLD X2, SINDA, BANYAN GOLD, ELEMENTAL ROYALTY AND MORE
snippet: The September 2026 semi-annual rebalancing of the MVIS Global Junior Gold Miners Index — the benchmark tracked by VanEck's GDXJ ETF ($9.3B AUM) — takes effect after market close today, September 18, forcing passive inflows into at least six new constituents: Gold X2, Sinda Ltd., Silver Storm Mining, Banyan Gold, Elemental Royalty Corp. and Mineros S.A.; GDXJ's mandatory buying at tonight's close is the catalyst retail investors who follow institutional positioning watch most closely in junior names, as front-running historically pushes new additions 3–5% above the rebalancing close in the week following inclusion.

headline: G MINING VENTURES CONFIRMS NEW GRODIOCAL GOLD DISCOVERY IN BRAZIL — TZ DEPTH DRILLING RETURNS 78M AT 1.81 g/t Au
snippet: G Mining Ventures Corp. (TSX: GMIN) released September 16 results from its dual-project Brazil exploration campaign — at Tocantinzinho, drilling 150 metres below the current pit design returned 78.1m at 1.81 g/t Au including 16.0m at 4.34 g/t Au, confirming mineralization continuity within a 15 km by 3 km mineralized corridor; maiden drilling at the new Grodiocal target within the Gurupi Project confirmed a near-surface gold discovery led by 23m at 1.97 g/t Au, with an updated Gurupi MRE and a Preliminary Economic Assessment both targeted for completion by year-end 2026.

headline: NICOLA MINING DRILLS FIRST-EVER HOLES AT BC SILVER MINE — TARGETS ZONE WITH SURFACE SAMPLES UP TO 1,300 g/t Ag
snippet: Nicola Mining Inc. (TSXV: NIM; NASDAQ: NICM) commenced its first-ever exploration drilling at the MB Zone of its Treasure Mountain silver property near Hope, BC on September 18, 2026 — a permitted silver-lead-zinc mine on care and maintenance since 2013; the 4-hole, ~800-metre program targets high-grade Ag-Pb-Zn with additional Cu and Au at a zone where surface sampling has returned up to 1,300 g/t silver, with assay results expected by year-end. CEO Peter Espig described the commencement as "a deliberate transition from asset preservation to value-oriented exploration."

headline: TERTIARY MINERALS DELINEATES 400M SILVER-COPPER ZONE IN ZAMBIA — 52M AT 99 g/t Ag WITH MRE TARGETED BEFORE YEAR-END
snippet: Tertiary Minerals PLC (AIM: TYM) outlined a ~400-metre-long higher-grade silver-copper-zinc mineralised zone at its Mushima North project in Zambia on September 18, 2026 — lead intercept of 52 metres at 99 g/t silver, 0.41% copper and 0.43% zinc at Target A1's Discovery Zone, with mineralisation confirmed open at depth beyond the existing 15–30 million tonne Exploration Target at 40–60 g/t silver equivalent; a new shallow copper zone returned 25 metres at 0.38% copper and the company is targeting a Mineral Resource Estimate before year-end 2026.

headline: ALBEMARLE +5.10%, SQM +4.54% AS LITHIUM PRICE STABILIZES — BIGGEST SINGLE-DAY GAIN IN WEEKS FOR SECTOR
snippet: The two largest lithium producers by market cap posted their biggest single-day gains in weeks on September 18 — Albemarle rising 5.10% to US$115.05 and SQM gaining 4.54% to US$71.80 with the LIT sector ETF adding 1.50%; market analysts attributed the moves to stabilization in Chinese lithium carbonate futures around 133,000–134,800 CNY/tonne after a 12.2% price decline from August's peak, with the day's price action suggesting the market may be finding a floor after months of demand-destruction pricing that has deferred significant production.

headline: KAZATOMPROM WON'T ACCELERATE OUTPUT AT ANY PRICE — SUPPLY DISCIPLINE TIGHTENS AN ALREADY-STRAINED URANIUM MARKET
snippet: A September 2026 analysis of Kazatomprom's strategy confirms the world's largest uranium producer will not increase output regardless of price signals — maintaining 2026 guidance at 27,500–29,000 tonnes on a 100% basis, with finished U3O8 inventory climbing 23% to 8,245 tU as of June 30, 2026; with US utilities covering less than 50% of the next decade's uranium requirements and the long-term contract price above $96.50/lb, Kazatomprom's price-insensitive supply posture is the single most important structural factor preventing the market from clearing in the near term.

headline: GOLD AT $4,400, JUNIOR MINES AT 0.51x P/NAV — WHY EXECUTION IS WHERE MINING RETURNS ARE WON OR LOST IN THIS CYCLE
snippet: A mid-September 2026 analysis by Discovery Alert argues that while gold sits above $4,400 and silver above $67, the junior and mid-cap mining sector trades at just 0.51x P/NAV — a gap the author attributes not to valuation error but to measurable execution risk; examples include Lafleur Minerals' first gold pour delayed to late Q4 2026 pending a C$30M Trafigura prepayment and J2 Metals' Sierra Plata project stalled by Mexico's 2023 mining law reforms, making the point that permitted and funded does not mean built — and that investors pricing juniors as if it does are systematically mispricing a historically recurring risk.
